title: Anna Paulina Luna revealed one detail about the House Epstein files release that shows how deep this really goes
text:
The Jeffrey Epstein scandal just got a whole lot bigger.
House Republicans finally got their hands on thousands of pages that previous administrations kept buried.
But Anna Paulina Luna revealed one detail about the House Oversight Committee’s Epstein files release that shows how deep this really goes.
The Trump administration hands over files to House Oversight After years of stonewalling by multiple administrations, the Department of Justice finally handed over 33,295 pages of Jeffrey Epstein records to the House Oversight Committee.
Chairman James Comer (R-KY) had to issue a subpoena just to get these documents that should have been public long ago.
This represents one of the biggest batches of Epstein records the government has ever made public and was announced just as Congressional members heard closed-door testimony from some of the Epstein victims this week.
Congresswoman Anna Paulina Luna (R-FL) broke down what’s actually in these files and some of what was revealed by victims in their testimony – and it’s worse than anyone imagined.
"Bigger than I think anyone anticipated," Luna posted on X after reviewing the materials.
The scope of this operation goes far beyond what the media has been willing to report.
Foreign governments were likely working with Epstein The Epstein network wasn’t just some rich guy’s sick hobby – it was an international trafficking operation with tentacles reaching into multiple governments.
"Foreign governments (as in more than one) were named to be working with Epstein," Luna revealed.
She didn’t stop there.
"It’s possible Jeffrey Epstein was an intelligence asset working for adversaries, and we must ask how much our own government knew," Luna stated.
Think about that for a second.
A convicted sex trafficker may have been working for hostile foreign powers while operating on American soil – and our intelligence agencies might have known about it, or even been involved.
The victims – some as young as 14 years old – described a "well orchestrated operation with many tentacles to include shell corporations" designed to move money and hide the true scope of the network.
Money trail to Deutsche Bank Here’s where it gets even more interesting.
Luna revealed that Congress is now following the money through a web of international banking that helped fund this operation.
"There is a lot to uncover ref the Deutsche Bank and how money was funneled and moved," Luna posted.
Chairman Comer is sending a Suspicious Activity Reports (SARS) request to the Treasury Department to trace exactly how this network was financed.
The victims told Congress that following the money is the key to understanding who was really behind this operation.
Luna made it clear: "There are very rich and powerful people that need to go to jail."
And they’re already scared.
"The attorneys of some of these implicated individuals have apparently already tried to contact some of the victims attorney’s," Luna revealed.
Even prison couldn’t stop Epstein The most disturbing revelation might be what happened while Epstein was supposedly being monitored by authorities.
"Epstein was still victimizing underaged girls while on work-release while wearing an ankle monitor, only to spend the evening in prison," Luna stated.
So much for the justice system protecting children.
The intimidation didn’t stop with Epstein’s death either.
"One victim had her newborn daughter threatened for coming forward," Luna revealed.
These people will stop at nothing to keep their secrets buried.
Congressional leadership is trying to thread a needle Luna made it crystal clear that Congress isn’t going to let this slide: "Rep Comer is running point on this and I am fully backing these efforts."
"The committee as a whole is working to ensure that they will be given access to their information that was previously denied to them by other admins," Luna explained.
She made sure to thank "the Trump admin for handing all of this over."
Previous administrations kept these files locked away while victims waited years for justice.
But another thing that is clear, which Luna may not have understood at the time, is that the manner in which Congressional leadership released the files fell short of full transparency.
The files – many of which will be heavily redacted it appears going by those reviewed thus far – were released on googledrive with backups on dropbox.
Instead of easily searchable pdf documents, the files appear to all be jpeg files for each individual page, meaning they are not easily parsed without being filtered through AI.
It will take some time to download all the files and quite a bit more for human eyes and minds to complete the painstaking task of combing through all the files and analysing their contents.
As a result, the public narrative about the files could be cast and cemented by the many mainstream media outlets and researchers who inevitably rely on AI to read and analyse the images.
The release came just ahead of Conservative Kentucky Congressman Thomas Massie’s filing of a discharge petition which would put legislation that requires the full release of the files on the floor for a vote – a move adamantly opposed by Washington, D.C. Swamp establishment figures in both parties.
The pushback to Massie’s call to release the full Epstein Files, as well as the limited, somewhat ham-fisted records released by the Oversight Committee suggests that data is woefully incomplete.
What this really means Look, here’s what all this tells us about the true scope of what we’re dealing with.
Some very powerful forces in both parties are trying to stop, delay, and obfuscate.
This wasn’t some isolated criminal enterprise – this was an international intelligence operation that may have compromised our own government agencies.
Foreign adversaries – or worse, supposed allies and even our own government – were potentially using a sex trafficking network to gather blackmail material on American officials and business leaders.
And the fact that attorneys for implicated individuals are already trying to intimidate victims shows how desperate the powerful people involved have become.
Luna didn’t mince words about where all of this should ultimately go, saying there are: "Very rich and powerful people that need to go to jail."
The question now is whether Congress has the backbone to see this investigation through to its conclusion – no matter how many powerful people get exposed.
